core: hue, value, and saturation or intensity
color systems in paint and screens

claims.claim: Color can be described through hue, value, and intensity or saturation.
Visual analysis can use color together with light, tone, form, line, texture, and pattern to describe a work before advancing an interpretation.
Traditional paint-media instruction commonly uses red, yellow, and blue primaries, whereas additive systems used by screens and many lights use red, green, and blue light.
Complementary colors are defined as opposite on a specified color wheel and are one of several color relationships a viewer can describe.
Color relationships can guide attention or connect areas of a composition, but formal observation alone cannot establish a universal response, cultural meaning, or maker intent.
Color observations can be affected by light, materials, display, and reproduction, so a viewer should identify the encounter being described.
